correctness.rationale: Completing the square gives formula (1) with the correct Fourier normalization and cosine phase. Factoring its positive cross amplitude gives two exact exponential envelope terms. A fixed-width O(1/T) boundary layer proves r<1/2 inside and r>1 outside; positivity of r double prime at frequencies comparable to T makes each negative cosine lobe strictly convex. Therefore exactly two simple zeros occur in every interior negative lobe and at most two counted with multiplicity in each edge lobe. Counting lobes gives the coefficient (b-a)^2/(a+b) and a uniform-in-delay bounded remainder for every fixed a<b,c>0. Five high-precision direct quadratures and fifteen numerical root-census cases agree; experiments are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural invariant is the cardinality of real Doppler nulls of the positive-pulse self-ambiguity at a given large delay, relevant to zero geometry in matched-filter and Gabor measurements. Despite each constituent Gaussian being zero-free, every fixed positive mixture of distinct widths develops quadratically many nulls; the exact growth coefficient depends only on the width disparity and is insensitive to mixing weight. The sharp two-sided moving wedge and convex interference-lobe mechanism control all roots up to O(1) and explain an otherwise hidden phase-space transition. This is not an arbitrary finite slice, restatement of the Gaussian integral, or a routine one-parameter numerical gain.
